clue.text: Temperature not-half cold during a picnic — drink warmer?

indicators.note: not half means only part of the following word survives, the first two of its four letters

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a picnic is something easy, as in 'it was no picnic'
the first half of the word cold

explanation.surface: A cold picnic outing where someone longs for a hot drink to warm them.
explanation.walkthrough: The half of 'cold' goes inside EASY, after T. The question mark flags that 'drink warmer' is a whimsical description, not a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cosy is a padded cover that keeps a teapot, and so the drink inside, hot.

clue.text: Country retreat almost entirely destroyed, one breaking in

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing a way inside, so the piece is inserted
something destroyed is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
almost entirely means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A war report: a country's retreat almost wiped out when one soldier breaks through.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last T, shuffle the rest, then put I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: 10 told to ___ lips and shut up!

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the words are judged by how they come out in speech

parts.note: the blank, said in a casual voice before lips, fits the command to keep your lips sealed
surface padding that completes the command to be quiet

explanation.surface: A girl being bluntly ordered to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal ya lips' is a colloquial 'seal your lips'; the girl's name fills the blank because it sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl, which is what 10 across is.

clue.text: Observed across the Midlands, primarily, university courses limited here

indicators.note: something stretched across another encloses it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: seen means observed

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letters of the words it follows

parts.note: first letters of these two words
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Something spotted across the Midlands, chiefly university courses being restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' looks academic beside university, but it means the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A set menu offers a fixed, restricted choice of dishes, the courses of a meal.

clue.text: Make a difference with effin' chow chow?

parts.note: to do good is to make a difference for the better
read as 'eff in': eff is how the letter F is spelt out, and in places it inside the phrase before it

explanation.surface: A sweary rant about eating the same chow over and over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effin'' disguises 'eff in': put F inside DO GOOD. A chow is a breed of dog, so 'chow chow' is a chow's chow, i.e. its food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow is slang for food and a chow is a dog breed, so a chow's chow is dog food.

clue.text: Old competition using one's trap?

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a rally is a motoring competition

explanation.surface: An old contest that involved setting a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orally means by mouth, and trap is a slang word for the mouth.

clue.text: Main warning, flag is gone, having been cut off

indicators.note: something that has gone is wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged
something cut off loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A ship's warning flag has been torn away and lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, a common crossword meaning. 'is' does double duty here in the surface but contributes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fog signal, such as a foghorn, warns ships at sea in poor visibility; the main is the open sea.

clue.text: Scoff too much duck, before opening barrel

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, zero

indicators.note: opening here means splitting open, so the piece goes inside the barrel

parts.note: a vat is a large barrel or tank
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A glutton gorging on duck before cracking open a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence the round letter; duck looks like the meat being scoffed.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily, so to scoff too much is to eat to excess.

clue.text: Indicators don't go round like that, going the opposite way of course

parts.note: needles are the pointers on dials and gauges

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to stay is not to go

indicators.note: travelling the opposite way means the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: so means like that, in that manner

explanation.surface: Car indicators that don't flash on a roundabout, or a driver heading the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indicators' and 'opposite way' paint a driving scene, but indicators here are the pointers on gauges.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course and the answer are both phrases meaning obviously, as anyone would expect.

parts.note: surface reading: just a pointer to the answer at 17 across, a female first name, with a question mark asking what it suggests
setter's reading: 17 is the name in a familiar hair accessory; replace that name with the generic word for a young female

explanation.walkthrough: An Alice band is a hairband. Swap the girl's name Alice for the word for any girl and you get a pop group of young women, the theme of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice band is a hair accessory; replacing the name with the generic noun for a female gives a female pop group, a cryptic leap.

clue.text: Ancient Egyptian winds blowing away a 10 27

parts.note: a Theban came from Thebes, the ancient Egyptian capital

indicators.note: the stated letter is blown out of the winds, so it is dropped

parts.note: gales are strong winds
taken as written, and removed from the winds

explanation.surface: Desert winds in Egypt sweep something away, with a nod to the band's hit Walk Like an Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 27' points at the theme entry, GIRL BAND. The Bangles were an American all-female group whose hit was Walk Like an Egyptian, hence the Egyptian surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bangles were a 1980s American pop group made up entirely of women.

clue.text: Fancy man's back in lecture

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is put inside another

parts.note: to orate is to speak at length, to lecture

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of man

explanation.surface: A dandy lounging at the back of a lecture hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborately decorated, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Instrument with drum beaten with malice when mum's away

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
mum is a mother, often called ma, and she goes missing from the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then losing MA

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a drum spitefully while their mother is out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum gives MA, which is removed from MALICE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dulcimer is a stringed instrument played by striking the strings with small hammers.

clue.text: Extremely excited, Posh and Ginger given cosmetic treatment

parts.note: manic means wildly excited
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U
ginger hair is red

explanation.surface: Posh and Ginger Spice, of the Spice Girls, getting excited over a beauty session.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh and Ginger were members of the Spice Girls, a girl band fitting the theme, but here they are just U and RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicured describes hands or nails that have had beauty treatment, trimmed and polished.

clue.text: Constant rain's ending, light aircraft having turned its back into it

indicators.note: turning round the back part of the word swaps its last two letters
into means going inside, so the pieces are put within the final word
the ending of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of rain
Cessna is a well-known maker of small light aircraft
taken as written

explanation.surface: Persistent rain eases off while a small plane turns round and heads into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the back of the plane's name is turned, swapping its last two letters, not the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant and the answer both mean continuing without pause.

clue.text: Join something that's enjoyable when stripped?

indicators.note: stripping something removes its outer layer, so only the inside letters remain

parts.note: something enjoyable is a fun item, which loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A question about something you like doing with your clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Something enjoyable is a FUN ITEM; strip off F and M to leave the answer. The stripping hint makes the surface look risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: To join things is to bring them together, which is a direct synonym of the answer as a verb.

clue.text: 3 another 10

indicators.note: another version of the name is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the answer to 3 down, a girl's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'another 10' does double work: 10 is GIRL, so this is another girl's name, and 'another' rearranges the letters of 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: What's lost on adopting alias? Fame ultimately

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
aka, also known as, introduces an alias

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of fame

explanation.surface: A celebrity taking a stage name wonders what they lose in the end for fame.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side of the field is also the leg side, so on gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the quantity that escapes or is lost through a leak.

clue.text: Rock like iron perhaps, but not lead thus rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way
the lead of a word is its first letter, and not means it is taken away

parts.note: iron is an example of a metal
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A rock sample resembles iron but contains no lead, so it is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead looks like the metal, which suits the iron surface, but it means the first letter. Rock looks like a stone; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to sway to and fro, and to oscillate is to swing back and forth.

clue.text: Challenge Dahl's giant's self-introduction?

parts.note: a self-introduction starts with I'm
Roald Dahl wrote James and the Giant Peach

explanation.surface: A query about how a giant in a Roald Dahl story would introduce itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Dahl's giant is not the BFG but the giant fruit of James and the Giant Peach, which would say 'I'm Peach'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach someone is to challenge their conduct or credibility, formally charging them.

clue.text: Take advantage of cheers riding horse

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: Enjoying the applause while riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'riding' puts one piece on top of the other. Cheers here means thanks, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap into something is to exploit or draw on it, to take advantage of it.

clue.text: Air type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tune or melody
second meaning: a breed or variety, as of a plant or virus

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare nouns; air is a tune here, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a musical melody and a variety or breed of an organism.

clue.text: Singer in fine voice inspiring group

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: alto is a singing voice
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A vocalist in great form, inspiring the rest of their band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fine voice' reads as a phrase meaning singing well, but it splits into fine and voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto can be a singer, usually male, who performs in an artificially high register.

clue.text: Sloppy fluid for tentacled invertebrates

indicators.note: fluid things have no fixed shape, so the letters flow into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Messy liquid suitable for feeding squishy sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyps are small aquatic animals such as hydras and coral, with a ring of tentacles around the mouth.

clue.text: Disrespectful words from name on Australian radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard, and an Australian voice shifts the vowel of the word

parts.note: a name or tag, said with an Australian vowel

explanation.surface: Insulting remarks broadcast about someone on an Australian radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian accent famously turns the long A of 'label' into something close to a long I.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is defamatory statements, so disrespectful words about a person qualify.

clue.text: Ass accompanying sheep in its noise as 10 27

indicators.note: in tells us the earlier pieces sit inside the following one

parts.note: the sheep's noise is a bleat
a nana is a fool, an ass
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A donkey and a sheep making a racket together in a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Nana is British slang for a fool. Bananarama were a British all-female pop trio of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananarama were a British pop group of women, so an instance of the theme entry.

clue.text: See 10
Writing of clues going down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crossword setter's work of composing a puzzle
second meaning: sinking, as the sun does in the evening

explanation.walkthrough: A wink at the setter's own job: crossword compilers are called setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Compilers set puzzles, and the sun sets when it sinks below the horizon, so both meanings share one verb form.

clue.text: Onion? There's no more, that's ___ !

indicators.note: this is the catchphrase announcing the end, which we must hear run together as spoken

parts.note: said quickly, the blank merges with that's into the phrase that's all, that's the lot

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that supplies have run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank and say the phrase aloud: 'that's shallot' runs together as 'that's all, (the) lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild variety of onion, so it is an example of the onion family.
